solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fish certainly from the right island

parts.note: to fish with rod and line is to angle

indicators.note: reading from the right means the word is taken right to left, backwards

parts.note: yes is an emphatic certainly

explanation.surface: An angler's tip: you can certainly catch fish off a particular island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the right' turns YES into SEY. ANGLESEY is an island off the north-west coast of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglesey is a Welsh island, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Garments from central Ukraine for Poles

indicators.note: central picks the middle letter of the word that follows

parts.note: pro is Latin for in favour of, for
N and S, the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Clothes sent from the middle of Ukraine to Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland, but means the north and south poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Aprons are protective garments tied over the front of clothes.

clue.text: Air force, leaders in aviation, for Swedish king

parts.note: a gust is a sudden force of moving air
the leading letters, the first two, of the word aviation

explanation.surface: The air force and aviation chiefs serve a Swedish monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air force' suggests the military; it is a blast of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav is the name of several kings of Sweden, such as Gustav Vasa.

clue.text: Finance some businessmen do without

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some business people manage without any funding.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to provide funds for, as with a college, so it means to finance.

clue.text: Cathedral on isle protected by tot up in heaven

parts.note: Ely is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: protected by means the isle letter is enclosed by the adding word

parts.note: to tot up is to add up, to sum
I is a standard abbreviation for isle or island

explanation.surface: A cathedral on an island is guarded by a child reaching up to heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' suggests a small child; 'tot up' means to add.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysium is the paradise of Greek myth, so it can mean heaven or bliss.

clue.text: French impudence is charming at first

parts.note: gall is cheeky boldness, impudence

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A remark that French cheek can be charming in the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallic is an adjective meaning of France or the French, a synonym.

clue.text: Aphrodite's bust may be wasted

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the goddess's name is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the goddess's name is the fodder; the possessive 's is not counted as letters

explanation.surface: A statue's bust of Aphrodite may be wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' suggests a sculpture of the goddess but means broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophied describes a body part wasted away through disuse.

clue.text: Pop art's leader in French newspaper

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the newspaper's name

parts.note: Le Monde is a leading Paris daily

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of the word art

explanation.surface: A French paper's lead feature on Pop Art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop art' reads as the movement; 'Pop' is the fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a fizzy soft drink, and lemonade is one such drink.

clue.text: Focus, say, on silver in the ancient city

parts.note: the Ford Focus is a model of car, so 'say' marks an example

indicators.note: in places the silver symbol inside the next word

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Concentrating, perhaps, on silver found in an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Focus' seems the verb; it is the Ford car model.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was a Phoenician city in North Africa destroyed by Rome.

clue.text: Playing darts? Yes, in leisure time

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they play darts says yes, in their free time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges DARTS and YES together.
explanation.definitionFit: Days off work are spent at leisure, so they are a form of free time.

clue.text: Salesman about to cross border for textbook

indicators.note: to cross means the turned word spans and encloses the border word
about here means turned round, so the salesman's word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman crosses a frontier to sell a textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the salesman's word backwards before the border word is set inside it; 'cross' here means span, not travel over.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is an elementary schoolbook teaching the basics, a kind of textbook.

clue.text: Place for eating hash

definitions.meaning: the dining room of soldiers or officers
to make a hash of is to make a muddle

explanation.surface: A hash served at an eating place.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is the military dining hall, and a mess is also a muddle or botch.

clue.text: Shade in weather that's changeable

indicators.note: changeable says the letters can be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A shady spot in weather that keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's changeable' rearranges IN and WEATHER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-white is a pale colour, and a colour can be called a shade.

clue.text: Appropriate amount of salt?

definitions.meaning: to appropriate is to take or steal, as a verb
a tiny quantity taken between finger and thumb, as of salt in cooking

explanation.surface: Asking what quantity of salt is the right one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective (suitable) but works as a verb meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is slang for to steal, and a pinch is the small amount of a seasoning held in the fingers.

clue.text: Uncle securing end of Auntie's clothes line?

indicators.note: securing means the uncle's name holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An uncle fixing his aunt's washing to the clothes line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes line' is not a washing line here but a line in clothes, where two pieces are stitched together.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the stitched join running along a garment, cryptically a line in clothes.

clue.text: Library slipping in limited edition for a lark

indicators.note: in sets the rearranged letters inside the shortened edition

parts.note: ed is the shortened form of edition

indicators.note: slipping suggests the letters slide out of place into a new order

explanation.surface: A library book slips into a limited edition just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipping' rearranges LIBRARY into ARLYBIR. 'limited' shortens edition to ED. 'for a lark' suggests fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is someone who rises early, just like an early riser or morning person.

clue.text: After climb, enjoy lively celebration

parts.note: to shin up is to climb using arms and legs
to dig something is slang for liking or enjoying it

explanation.surface: Climb first, then have fun at a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal noisy party, a lively celebration.

clue.text: Deny policeman's allegation

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, plus the possessive S
an allegation is a claim

explanation.surface: Rejecting a police officer's accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclaim something is to disown or refuse to admit it.

clue.text: Girl put up articles in French college

parts.note: Emma is a girl's name

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the words are written upwards, backwards

parts.note: le and un are the French definite and indefinite articles
un is the French indefinite article, a

explanation.surface: A girl puts up some articles written in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns LE UN into NUEL. Emmanuel College is in Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel is one of the Cambridge University colleges.

clue.text: This writer's by lake holding one wing of sitting duck

parts.note: the setter referring to themself: I'm, short for I am

indicators.note: holding means the lake word contains the next piece

parts.note: a mere is a small lake

indicators.note: one wing of means a letter from one side, here the first, of the next word

explanation.surface: The writer sits by a lake holding a duck that is a sitting target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird from 'sitting duck' but is the verb, to plunge under water.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to dip them under water, and to immerse is to submerge.

clue.text: Formerly employed in power station

indicators.note: employed in says the letters are used within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone who used to work at a power plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Erst is an archaic adverb meaning once or long ago.

clue.text: Firm American lawyer closing bars

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A US legal firm's attorney is shutting down drinking bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs, but these are musical bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a musical piece, its final measures.

clue.text: Officer liable to plug marked man

indicators.note: to plug means to fill a hole, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Cain bore the mark of God after killing Abel
apt means likely or liable to

explanation.surface: An officer who is prone to shoot a targeted man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug' suggests shooting; it means filling a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a commissioned rank in the army or navy.

clue.text: One drink after another for horse

definitions.meaning: a drink taken straight after a different one
a horse trained for steeplechase racing

explanation.surface: Drinking one after another for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser follows a drink, and a steeplechaser is a jumping racehorse.

clue.text: Deliver from sin in exchange for cash?

definitions.meaning: to save a soul, in religious terms
to cash in a voucher or bond

explanation.surface: Asking whether salvation can be paid for.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ is said to save sinners, and pawned goods or bonds are bought back or cashed in.

clue.text: Cautious cleaner back from holiday

parts.note: a char is a British term for a cleaning lady, a charwoman

indicators.note: back from picks the rear, final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A wary cleaner has just returned from a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back from holiday' suggests returning from a trip; it gives the last letter of holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Chary is a synonym for wary or careful about risk.

clue.text: Tomb involving curse? Help!

indicators.note: involving suggests letters wound or tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in a cursed tomb crying out for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' rearranges CURSE and HELP together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepulchre is a burial vault or chamber, a tomb.

clue.text: Wind up in coils

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to spool is to wind thread on a reel

explanation.surface: Winding something up into coils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' reads as one phrase; 'up' turns SPOOL around.
explanation.definitionFit: Loops are rings or curls, so coils is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Representation of Nubia's god

indicators.note: a representation is a new rendering, so the letters are set out differently

parts.note: the possessive's S is counted as a letter of the fodder here

explanation.surface: A statue or image of the deity worshipped in Nubia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representation of' rearranges NUBIAS, including the S of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Anubis is the jackal-headed Egyptian deity of the dead, an example of a deity.

clue.text: Blind one escaping from prison and falling into river

indicators.note: escaping means the letter gets out of the prison word
falling into means that letter drops inside the river word

parts.note: jail is a prison
the Ouse is a river in England, flowing through York
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A blind prisoner escapes and tumbles into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The I leaves JAIL (giving JAL) and falls into OUSE (giving OUSIE). 'Blind' is the noun, a window shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalousie is a window shutter with angled slats, a type of window blind.

clue.text: Complaint of young man in springtime

indicators.note: in means the young man sits inside the month

parts.note: May is a month of spring
a lad is a boy or young man

explanation.surface: A young man's grumble in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' suggests a grievance but means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an ailment or illness, which is a malady.

clue.text: Gram's not new measure in physics

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the S of the possessive is counted as a letter here

explanation.surface: A claim that the gram is not a newly invented physics unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not new' reads as one phrase, but NOT is fodder and 'new' rearranges GRAMS and NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The angstrom is a tiny unit of length used for atomic distances in physics.
